### 7.19 Honey Chicken Marinade & Kabobs

Transcribed from Cody's spreadsheet — a simple honey-soy marinade for grilled chicken, built out into a full kabob spread with the fruit, vegetables, and kielbasa he listed alongside it. Rated **"Yummie"** on the sheet itself.

> ✅ 2026-09-07 per Cody ("use your judgment") — **two kinds of skewer, and a 4-to-6-hour marinade.** Cody's words: the **kielbasa** goes with the zucchini, onions, tomatoes, and squash; the **chicken** goes with *a lot of pineapple*; and it's a 4-to-6-hour marinade — *"you don't really marinate chicken overnight, do you?"* So the build below is **Skewer A: chicken and pineapple** and **Skewer B: kielbasa and vegetables**, and the old "overnight is fine" is gone. **Quantities for the pineapple, zucchini, squash, tomatoes, and kielbasa weren't on the original sheet** — only the item names were listed, with amounts given for the marinade, chicken, garlic, onion, and bell pepper. The amounts and cut sizes for those five are **cookbook judgment**, sized to 8 breast halves' worth of skewers and checked against America's Test Kitchen's grilled chicken kebabs (1-inch cubes, 3–6 hr marinade, ~3 min per side over direct heat; https://www.americastestkitchen.com/recipes/3027-grilled-chicken-kebabs and https://www.americastestkitchen.com/recipes/16949-go-to-grilled-chicken-kebabs) and Food Network Kitchen's (https://www.foodnetwork.com/recipes/food-network-kitchen/grilled-chicken-kebabs-3812068). The sheet's ingredient list (column A–C) also includes a second, unquantified "onions" line beyond the 5 small onions already called for — ✅ **closed 2026-09-08: it's the same onions.** Cody: *"I don't know what the duplicated onions are, so just use your judgment, because you're just quartering onions there."* One onion line, quartered.

> ✅ **2026-09-08 — the kebab build is Cody's, in his own pattern.** He walked the skewer piece by piece: **kielbasa, a quarter of an onion, kielbasa, a tomato, kielbasa, an onion, a piece of zucchini, kielbasa** — **roughly 35–40% kielbasa**, so the sausage sits against a vegetable everywhere along the skewer and its juice runs into all of them. **Tomato and zucchini are the vegetables he names**, and they're marked as his additions below rather than as cookbook judgment. **Season the vegetables liberally with Cavender's Greek seasoning, and the chicken too** — *"season it to taste."* Steps 4, 6, and 7 carry all of it. **The one number that's still the cookbook's** is the kielbasa quantity, raised from 1½ lb to **2 lb** so there's actually enough sausage to build his ratio at four rounds a skewer.

**🟡 Medium** · **Prep ~40 min** *(all the cutting and skewering)* · **Cook ~12 min** · **Start to finish ~5–7 hr** *(4–6 hr marinate)*

**⏰ Countdown to dinner:** T−5 to 7 hr whisk the marinade, cube the chicken, into the bag in the fridge — 4 to 6 hr, not overnight · T−1 hr cut the pineapple, onions, tomatoes, zucchini, peppers and squash; slice the kielbasa; thread Skewer A (chicken and pineapple) and Skewer B (kielbasa alternating with vegetables); Cavender's liberally on both (soak wooden skewers 30 min first) · T−45 min light the grill, direct medium-high, 400–450°F, grates oiled · T−15 min Skewer A on, 10–12 min, turning every 3; Skewer B on 2 min later, 8–10 min · T−0 chicken at 160–165°F, both off together.

**❤️ Family favorite** — *Cody: "Freaking awesome."*

#### A. Ingredients

**Marinade**

- ¼ cup olive oil
- ⅓ cup honey
- ⅓ cup soy sauce
- ¼ tsp ground black pepper
- 2 cloves garlic, minced

**Skewer A — chicken & pineapple** *(about 10 skewers)*

- 8 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves (about 3 lb), cut into 1-inch cubes
- 2 whole pineapples, cored and cut into 1-inch chunks *(cookbook judgment — "a lot of pineapple," per Cody; one pineapple gives 40–50 chunks and you want one per chicken cube)*

**Skewer B — kielbasa & vegetables** *(about 8 skewers)*

- **2 lb kielbasa (kalbasa), sliced into 1-inch rounds** — *the amount is cookbook judgment, raised from 1½ lb on 2026-09-08 to feed the build Cody described: **roughly 35–40% of the skewer is kielbasa**, which takes about 4 rounds per skewer*
- **5 small onions, quartered** — *quartered onion is what goes on the skewer, per Cody, 2026-09-08*
- **2 large tomatoes, cut into quarters** — ✅ *Cody's own, 2026-09-08: tomato is one of the two vegetables he names by name on the skewer* *(large tomatoes, not cherry — his call)*
- **2 medium zucchini, cut into ¾-inch rounds** — ✅ *Cody's own, 2026-09-08: the other vegetable he names on the skewer*
- 2 red bell peppers, cut into 2-inch pieces
- 2 medium yellow squash, cut into ¾-inch rounds *(cookbook judgment — on the sheet's list, but not named in his skewer build)*

**Both**

- **Greek seasoning** — **Cavender's**, the one Cody names. ✅ *2026-09-08:* **hit the vegetables liberally with it, and the chicken too.** His measurement is *"season it to taste"* — there isn't a number and there doesn't need to be one
- Skewers *(about 18; soak wooden ones 30 min)*

#### B. Cooking Instructions

**1. Make the marinade.**
Whisk the olive oil, honey, soy sauce, black pepper, and minced garlic together in a bowl until combined. This is about 1 cup — the right amount for 3 lb of chicken.

**2. Marinate the chicken. 4 to 6 hours in the refrigerator — not overnight.**
Cube the chicken and toss it with the marinade in a zip-top bag, press the air out, and refrigerate. **Four to six hours is the window, per Cody.** Two hours will still pick up flavor if you're short; past six the soy starts curing the surface rather than flavoring it, and the texture goes drier and hammier — which is why it doesn't go overnight. Discard the bag and the marinade when the chicken comes out.

**3. Cut the fruit and vegetables.**
Pineapple in 1-inch chunks to match the chicken. Onions quartered, bell peppers in 2-inch pieces, zucchini and squash in ¾-inch rounds — all roughly the same size so Skewer B finishes evenly. Cut the tomatoes into **quarters**, chunkier than wedges, so they hold together longer on the fire.

**4. Slice the kielbasa.**
Kielbasa is already fully cooked, so it's not marinating with the chicken — it just needs 1-inch rounds thick enough to blister and pick up char without drying out. **A 2-lb rope gives about 32 rounds, four per skewer**, which is what Cody's alternating build needs.

**5. Thread Skewer A: chicken and pineapple, one for one.**
Alternate **1 chicken cube, 1 pineapple chunk** — about 6 chicken and 5–6 pineapple per skewer, packed snug so the pineapple bastes the chicken. That's the whole skewer; no vegetables on this one. Makes about 10.

**6. Thread Skewer B: alternate kielbasa and vegetables the whole way down — sausage, vegetable, sausage, vegetable.**
✅ **2026-09-08 — this is Cody's own build, and he gave the pattern piece by piece:** **kielbasa, a quarter of an onion, kielbasa, a tomato, kielbasa, an onion, a piece of zucchini, kielbasa.** That's the shape of it — **you're putting a round of sausage between the vegetables all the way along**, not grouping the sausage at one end or clustering the vegetables together. **He puts it at roughly 35 to 40 percent kielbasa**, which is what that pattern actually comes to: it's close to one-for-one by piece, but a 1-inch round of sausage is a smaller thing than a quartered onion, so by bulk the sausage lands around a third of the skewer. **Four rounds per skewer is the working number.** Makes about 8. Bell pepper and yellow squash ride along in the vegetable slots the same way.

*✅ **Why the alternation matters — this is a technique, not a loading order, and it's the reason the skewer is worth eating.** Cody's own reasoning is that the sausage juice has to run into the vegetables, and that only happens if there's sausage touching them everywhere. Kielbasa is fully cooked and fatty, so on the fire it doesn't absorb — it **gives**. The rendered fat and juice have to go somewhere, and whatever is pressed against it catches them. **An onion quarter is the best thing on the skewer for that job** — its layers separate slightly as they soften and drink it in, and you end up with an onion that tastes like the sausage — but tomato and zucchini do the same thing, which is exactly why they're threaded between rounds rather than beside each other. **Sandwich a vegetable between two kielbasa rounds wherever you can** so it's picking up juice from both sides. The tomato benefits twice over: mid-skewer between two rounds, the sausage also shields it from the direct flame. It will still soften; that's fine on a skewer that only needs 8–10 minutes.*

**7. Season both skewer types liberally with Greek seasoning (Cavender's) before they hit the grill.**
✅ **2026-09-08 per Cody: hit the vegetables liberally with Cavender's, and the chicken too.** His measurement is *"season it to taste"* — take that as the instruction it is, not as a missing number. Be generous with it: this is a shake-on-and-grill seasoning, and the fire and the fat both take the edge off it, so what looks like too much in the bowl reads about right off the grill. **The onions can take more than anything else** — heavily seasoned onion plus rendered kielbasa juice is the best bite on Skewer B. The chicken has already been in the honey-soy marinade, so it needs less than the vegetables do, but it still gets some.

**8. Grill over direct medium-high, about 400–450°F, grates oiled. Skewer A 10–12 minutes, Skewer B 8–10.**
Start Skewer A first. Turn every 3 minutes so all four sides see the fire — the honey will blacken at the edges, and that's the look, but if it's charring hard before the 8-minute mark, slide them to a cooler zone. **Chicken is done at 160–165°F in the thickest cube.** Put Skewer B on about 2 minutes after A and turn it the same way; it's done when the kielbasa is blistered and the squash is tender with char. Both come off together. Serve hot, off the skewers or on them.

#### C. Grocery Shopping List

**🛒 General grocery**

- 🛒 Olive oil — ¼ cup
- 🛒 Honey — ⅓ cup
- 🛒 Soy sauce — ⅓ cup
- 🛒 Ground black pepper
- 🛒 Garlic — 2 cloves
- 🛒 Skinless, boneless chicken breast — 8 halves (about 3 lb)
- 🛒 Pineapple — 2 whole
- 🛒 Kielbasa (kalbasa) — **2 lb** *(raised from 1½ lb on 2026-09-08 — the skewer runs 35–40% sausage, about 4 rounds each)*
- 🛒 Small onions — 5 *(quartered for the skewer)*
- 🛒 Tomatoes (large, not cherry) — 2 *(✅ named by Cody as a skewer vegetable, 2026-09-08)*
- 🛒 Zucchini — 2 medium *(✅ named by Cody as a skewer vegetable, 2026-09-08)*
- 🛒 Red bell peppers — 2
- 🛒 Yellow squash — 2 medium
- 🛒 Greek seasoning — **Cavender's** *(Cody's pick; buy the big shaker, the onions take a lot of it)*
- 🛒 Skewers — about 18
